title: The Chase
paragraphs: An NBC dramatic anthology in which every story is built around a pursuit or race against danger, moving freely among crime, adventure, suspense, and occasional science fiction.
NBC dramatic anthology built around hunter/hunted situations across crime, adventure, suspense, fantasy, horror and occasional science fiction.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: NBC sustaining run (April 27, 1952 to June 28, 1953) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Lawrence Klee (writer, creator, and director), Fred Collins (announcer), Fred Weihe (director and transcriber), Edward King (director and transcriber), Leon Janney (performer), Roger De Koven (performer), and Daniel Sutter (director and transcriber).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]].

The stories often return to pursuit, escape and hunter/hunted situations, murder and homicide, fraud, blackmail and financial schemes, espionage, Cold War and international intrigue, science fiction and speculative threats, and ghosts and supernatural threats.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes NBC sustaining anthology production, Cold War-era pursuit stories, and Cross-genre anthology experimentation.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]], [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]], [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]], [[show|dimension-x|Dimension X]], and [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]].
